newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude steady in NYMEX ACCESS after-hour trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude steady in NYMEX ACCESS after-hour trade.

text.p: U.S. crude oil futures held onto gains from the sizzling floor session in active trade on Monday that opened the evening's ACCESS after-hours session.

NYMEX January crude eased slightly to $24.76 a barrel, giving back 4 cents a barrel on 1,081 lots traded, including 534 in the front-month contract. Fueled by a rally in gasoline futures, January crude had settled up $1.05 a barrel at $24.80 in the earlier floor session.
"Looking at the bid and asked (prices), I don't see (crude prices) moving much either way," one trader said.

January gasoline was bid 67.80 cents a gallon, asked 68.10 cents after setting a new contract high at 68.28 cents early in the session. A modest 111 lots were traded, including 71 in the front-month contract, early in the session.

January heating oil opened at 73.35 cents a gallon, and sellers were asking 73.50 cents on 99 lots traded, including 84 in the front-month contract. The contract had finished 1.89 cents a gallon higher at 73.57 cents in the floor session.
